note: Verifies CLI dialect-dispatch and cross-tool behavior of Microsoft Coreutils 2026.6.16 on native Windows, against System32 / PowerShell / Git Bash baselines. These are pass/fail behavior observations, not a timing distribution. Source of truth for reproduction: run.sh -> probe.sh output. Observed 2026-06-26 (see manifest.backfilled).

behaviors_verified.claim: The SAME binary picks DOS vs Unix dialect from argument SHAPE, not just argv0. `find.exe . -type f` walks the tree (GNU); `find.exe /C "apple" crlf.txt` returns the DOS match-count line. `sort.exe -n` is GNU numeric; `sort.exe /R` is DOS reverse.
behaviors_verified.evidence: probe.sh steps find-gnu / find-dos / sort-gnu / sort-dos
behaviors_verified.confirms: The reported nthelpers.rs heuristic (/C /N -> DOS; -name/-n/+N -> GNU; ambiguous -> DefaultFind/DefaultSort registry; default DOS) is confirmed firsthand.

behaviors_verified.claim: coreutils `find` (file-tree walk) and System32 `find.exe` (in-file string search) are semantically OPPOSITE. Feeding a GNU-style invocation to System32 find mis-parses it.

observed.System32 find . -name *.txt: Access denied - . / File not found - -NAME (total misread)

behaviors_verified.claim: The binary does its own Windows-CRT argv globbing, which cmd does not. `coreutils echo *.txt` expands to filenames, and that same expansion BREAKS `find . -name *.txt` (pattern gets replaced by the file list).

observed.powershell -name '*.txt': breaks again (single token passed without surviving quotes)

behaviors_verified.caveat: Quote-survival differs per shell (cmd vs PowerShell), so the same command line is not portable across Windows shells.

behaviors_verified.claim: Numeric sort splits three ways. coreutils `sort -n` is true numeric; everything else defaults to lexicographic on this fixture.
coreutils sort is locale-aware, and `LC_ALL=C` does NOT force byte order on it — so the classic CI determinism trick `LC_ALL=C sort` may not behave like GNU/Git-Bash sort.
behaviors_verified.evidence: probe.sh step collation (bytes confirmed via od on OS redirect)
behaviors_verified.excluded_from_post: A single-char Z/a/B/b input made default sort emit a mojibake 3-byte UTF-8 sequence — reproducible but unexplained edge anomaly; deliberately NOT used as a claim in the post (honesty).

behaviors_verified.claim: Line-ending handling differs by utility: grep normalizes (strips \r), sort preserves (keeps \r\n). wc counts newlines correctly and exposes the CRLF byte delta.
behaviors_verified.evidence: probe.sh step crlf (output bytes via od)

behaviors_verified.claim: coreutils grep 0.1.0 does ERE (-E) and PCRE (-P, Oniguruma), but has no LANG/localization yet.
behaviors_verified.caveat: grep 0.1.0 is early: LANG encoding not honored, no localization; i18n needs separate verification.

approximate_not_a_claim.note: Single warm run on a 600k-line / 28.6MB file. Timing is hardware- and cache-dependent and is NOT committed as a benchmark number — the post states performance is 'same order of magnitude', not a win.

honest_limits: GA vs preview tension: Build 2026 blog says GA, GitHub README still carries preview wording (early service release).
GNU test-suite compat numbers are Linux-execution figures, not Windows end-to-end. See manifest.cited_not_measured.
/dev/null->NUL, no POSIX signals, permissions are ACL (not POSIX bits), symlink creation needs Developer Mode / elevation.
Backslash path output can break Linux-style `grep "/src/"` pipelines.
Not a WSL replacement (complementary); shares roles with Git Bash / MSYS2.

Shims reproduced via argv0 copies (real install uses hardlinks) — behavior identical, but PATH/registry/PowerShell-profile integration was NOT installed, so that part is cited from Microsoft docs, not measured.
